<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 23:22">Targ. Prov. XXIII, 22</cite> <he>יַלְדָּךְ</he> who begot thee.
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 17:19">Targ. Gen. XVII, 19</cite> <he>תְּלִיד</he>; usu. <he>תֵּילַד</he>, <he>תֵּלַד</he>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 22:32">Targ. Ps. XXII, 32</cite> <he>למֵילַד</he> to create; a. v. fr.—

<cite ref="Bava Batra 91a:12">B. Bath. 91ᵃ</cite> (prov.) <he>בחייך דיַלְדַּת שיתין למה לך דיַלְדַּת</he> Ms. M. (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) by thy life, the sixty (weaklings) thou begottest, what didst thou beget them for? <he>איכפיל ואוֹלִיד וכ׳</he> (v. infra) marry again and beget one as strong as sixty; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 66">Yalk. Jud. 66</cite>.

<cite ref="Makkot 17b:2">Macc. 17ᵇ</cite> <he>דִּילִידָא אימיה כר״ש תֵּילוֹד</he> whose mother soever is with child may she bear a son like R. S.; Yalk. Deut. <he>כל דיַלְדָּה אימה כר״ש תְּלִיד</he>; a. v. fr.
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 4:18">Targ. Gen. IV, 18</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Yevamot 76a:13">Yeb. 76ᵃ</cite> <he>בר אוֹלוּדֵי</he> capable of begetting; <cite ref="Yevamot 76a">ib.</cite> <he>בני אולודי</he>.
<cite ref="Eruvin 104a">Erub. 104ᵃ</cite> is it not because <he>דקמוֹלִיד קלא וכל אולודי וכ׳</he> he produces a sound, and every production of sound is forbidden (on the Sabbath)?; a. fr.
<cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 1:16">Targ. Ex. I, 16</cite>.—
<cite ref="Sotah 11b:19">Sot. 11ᵇ</cite> <he>לאוֹלוּדָהּ</he> to deliver her.

senses.gloss: to act as midwife. Y. Keth. V, 30ᵃ bot. [read:] דמְיַלְּדָא, v. חֲכַם.

units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 144:13">Targ. Ps. CXLIV, 13</cite>.

senses.gloss: to be born, to grow, to come forth.
units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 78:6">Targ. Ps. LXXVIII, 6</cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 4:26">Targ. Gen. IV, 26</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 136a">Sabb. 136ᵃ</cite> <he>א׳ ליה וכ׳</he> a child was born to him.
<cite ref="Beitzah 2b:9">Bets. 2ᵇ</cite> <he>כל ביצה דמִתְיַילְּדָא האידנא וכ׳</he> (some ed. <he>דמִתְיְילִידָא</he>) an egg laid to-day was fully developed yesterday.
<cite ref="Beitzah 2b:12">Ib.</cite> <he>הנך דמִתְיְלִידָן וכ׳</he> those laid on the same day.
<cite ref="Chullin 9a:10">Ḥull. 9ᵃ</cite> <he>אִתְיְלִידָא בה ריעותא</he> (not <cite ref="J00368"><he>אתיליד</he></cite>) an accident occurred to it which made the case suspicious.
<cite ref="Nedarim 30b:11">Ned. 30ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <he>נולדים</he>, Mish.

ib. III, 9, v. preced.) למימרא … דמִתְיַילְּדָן משמע does this mean to say that noladim means ‘things which will be forthcoming’?; אלא מעתה … ה״נ דמִתְיַילְּדִין הוא (v. marginal note) if this be so, does hannoladim in Gen. XLVIII, 5 also mean ‘those to be born’? ואלא מאי דִיְּילִידוּ משמע (= דְּאִיְּילִידוּ Ithpe. contr.) but what else? Does it (always) mean ‘those that have been born’?
